summary: The UAE procures large solar and storage projects through state-run competitive tenders with long fixed-price PPAs, a model in place for almost 30 years. Direct corporate PPAs and third-party access are limited, and foreign ownership is restricted in some cases.

access.reason: EWEC in Abu Dhabi and DEWA in Dubai run competitive IPP tenders for large solar and storage projects.

terms.reason: PPAs have fixed prices with agreed escalation for their whole term, which lets developers raise limited recourse finance.

buyer.reason: The offtakers EWEC and DEWA are state-owned.

ownership.reason: There are restrictions on foreign ownership in some cases, and sovereign funds often co-invest in projects.

stability.reason: The PPA model has been used for almost 30 years, and no retroactive change was found.

direction.reason: Record projects such as the 5.2 GW solar and 19 GWh battery plant are under way.

access.reason: Direct corporate PPAs and third-party access are limited, but rooftop solar through Shams Dubai suits smaller businesses.

ownership.reason: Foreign ownership is restricted in some cases.

build.reason: Grid connection is constrained for distributed generation, and a 2022 federal law regulates linking such units to the grid.

direction.reason: Corporate PPAs and off-site purchasing are emerging.

events.title: Federal law regulates connecting distributed renewable units to the grid

sources.title: Renewable Energy, United Arab Emirates (comparative guide)
Renewable energy in the United Arab Emirates

gaps: Grid connection times and the exact foreign ownership rules for energy companies were not covered by the sources reviewed.
